rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The frog's reproductive system is adapted for external fertilisation in water. The male has two kidney-shaped testes, vasa deferentia, seminal vesicles, and a cloaca (no copulatory organ). The female has two lobed ovaries, oviducts that add a jelly coat, a uterus, and a cloaca. During amplexus, the male grasps the female and both release gametes into the water, where external fertilisation occurs.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Male: testes → vasa deferentia → seminal vesicles → cloaca
Female: ovaries → oviducts (jelly coat) → uterus → cloaca
Fertilisation: external (in water) during amplexus

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Frogs have EXTERNAL fertilisation (in water), NOT internal.  ·  The male does NOT have a copulatory organ; he releases sperm over the eggs during amplexus.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects labelled male and female reproductive diagrams.  ·  External fertilisation + amplexus is a very common long-answer.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Male: testes (2, kidney-shaped) → vasa deferentia → seminal vesicles → cloaca.  ·  Female: ovaries (2, lobed) → oviducts (with jelly gland) → uterus → cloaca.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: External fertilisation  ·  Amplexus  ·  Male reproductive organs  ·  Female reproductive organs

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Male: 2 kidney-shaped testes; vasa deferentia; seminal vesicles; cloaca; no copulatory organ.  ·  Female: 2 lobed ovaries; oviducts (with jelly coat); uterus; cloaca.  ·  External fertilisation in water during amplexus.  ·  Amplexus: male grasps female (axillary in Rana).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Frogs lay 5,000–20,000 eggs at a time; most do not survive, but external fertilisation ensures high numbers.  ·  Amplexus (the male's grip on the female) is unique to most frogs; it is absent in most salamanders.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain external fertilisation and amplexus.  ·  Describe the development of the frog from egg to adult.  ·  State the ecological importance of frogs.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Describe the development from egg to adult.  ·  Protista and Protozoa is frequently tested.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Amplexus: male (axillary) grasps female; egg + sperm release in water.  ·  Development: zygote → blastula → gastrula → tadpole (gills + tail) → froglet → adult (lungs, no tail).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Frog fertilisation is: → B  ·  The male's grip on the female during reproduction is called: → B

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Male reproductive system: testes (2, kidney-shaped, along the dorsal wall) → vasa deferentia → seminal vesicles → cloaca; no copulatory organ.  ·  Female reproductive system: ovaries (2, lobed, along the dorsal wall) → oviducts (funnel-shaped opening near the kidney) → uterus → cloaca.  ·  Eggs: unfertilised ova are released into the oviducts; the oviduct adds a jelly coat; eggs are deposited in water.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Jelly coat on eggs  ·  Metamorphosis (tadpole → adult)  ·  Bio-indicator role

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: No copulatory organ  ·  Kingdom protista (Gr; protistos, first of all) was proposed by Ernst Haeckel in 1866.  ·  Later, an American taxonomist Robert Harding Whittaker broadly divided all the living beings of this universe into five kingdoms in 1969 basically on the basis of phylogenetic relationship among them.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: 1 Five kingdom classification Protistans consist of microscopic, single-celled and primitive eukaryotic organisms.  ·  This group includes diverse living organisms that are plant-like, such as golden algae and diatoms, animals like such as Paramecium and Amoeba.  ·  Some of them are both plants and animals like such as Euglena and Astasia and some of them are fungi like such as Fuligo, Protostelium, etc.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Development: zygote → blastula → gastrula → tadpole → metamorphosis → adult  ·  Development: egg → zygote → tadpole (gills + tail) → adult (lungs, no tail).  ·  Economic: pest control; ecological: water quality bio-indicator.
